newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FALDO TAKES LEAD AT NISSAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FALDO TAKES LEAD AT NISSAN OPEN.

text.p: Nick Faldo birdied the first three holes at the Riviera Country Club Saturday en route to a three-under-par 68 and a one-stroke lead after the third round of the Nissan Open.
The Briton also birdied the seventh hole, a shot he gave back with a bogey at 14.
"I was very pleased with my start," said Faldo, who is seeking his sixth victory on the PGA Tour. "But I didn't quite keep my momentum going. I didn't squeeze anything else out of it."

Through 54 holes, Faldo was at nine-under-par 204. Scott McCarron and defending champion Craig Stadler were tied for second, one stroke behind Faldo. McCarron shot a seven-under 64 that included back-to-back eagles at the 10th and 11th holes. Stadler shot a 68.
Lurking within striking distance four strokes back were Fred Couples, a two-time winner of the event, and Mark O'Meara, seeking to win a third straight PGA Tour event.
Tiger Woods shot a 72 and was eight shots off the lead.
Faldo has not won a tournament since winning the Masters last April.
"I had a lot of things in my life off the golf course that had to be taken care of," he said. "Golf was way down the list. Now everything is sorted out and golf is back to my only priority."
McCarron vaulted into contention when he holed a 45-foot chip for eagle at the par-four 10th hole and a 25-foot chip for eagle at the par-five 11th hole. He used an eight-iron for each shot.
"I'm going to be sleeping with my eight-iron tonight," he said.
